Make Comparison with Not as… as

When we want to say that two things are not equal, we use the form “as …as”. The structure is the following:
not + as + adjective + as
Object code is not as easy to modify as source code.

It helps protect valuable intellectual property, and, since they are not as good at working with source code as programmers, customers are prone to purchase software maintenance and other services from the vendor.
However, the customer sometimes may not need the vendor's help to get required software maintenance services as it may not be as convenient as established in the software license agreement.
When using this structure, we establish that the first thing mentioned is “less” than the second thing.
Example:
Source code isn't as easy as other programming languages.
This structure is also used to compare actions.
Example:
That source code escrow arrangement didn't work as well as we expected.
Understanding the Concept of Source Code Escrow
Source code escrow happens when the sourced code of sotware is deposited with a third party escrow agent. This escrow is demanded by the licensee to ensure software maintenance and technical support.

The licensed software code is provided to the licensee if the vendor files for bankruptcy or is not able to maintain or update the software as established in the software license agreement.

Keeping software updated is essential for most companies and they usually would like to make sure that software maintenance continues even if the vendor is not capable to do so. The best way to achieve this is by accessing the software source code; however, as this is usually protected as intellectual property, source code escrow makes sure the licensee obtain access to the source code only when the vendor fails to provide software maintenance.

A source code escrow agreement usually:
  • Specifies the subject and scope of the escrow.
  • Ensures the vendor puts updated versions of the software.
  • Specifies the conditions under which the source code may be released to the licensee.
  • Specifies services provided by the escrow agent besides the custody of the source code.

Source Code Escrow Arrangements

A source code escrow arrangement is often included in software license agreements so the customer can access and use source code for the licensed software in case any event occurs. Events, also known as “release events” occur because of the software vendor's bankruptcy or its breach of its contractual obligation to procure software maintenance services.
The software is usually written in a language that only well-versed programmers can understand and modify. The final version of the computer software is “source code” and is gathered into machine language format known as “object code”. Object code is difficult to be understood and modified. Therefore, programmers need to have access to the source code. Object code is not as easy to modify as source code.

Object code distribution happens when software vendors give customers software in this format. It helps protect valuable intellectual property, and, since they are not as good at working with source code as programmers, customers are prone to purchase software maintenance and other services from the vendor. However, the customer sometimes may not need the vendor's help to get required software maintenance services as it may not be as convenient as established in the software license agreement. In such a case the customer may ask for a supplemental remedy supplied through a source code escrow arrangement.

The need for a source code escrow arrangement will depend on:
  • How important the licensed software is for the customer and the cost and time it would take them to replace it.
  • How likely it is for the vendor to fail at providing software maintenance services
  • How good are the deposited source code and related materials.
  • How capable the customer is to use the source code to maintain the licensed software.
